items.title: swyx: low reasoning effort plus a critique loop beats max effort
items.takeaway: For throughput-bound work, run cheaper settings and check outputs with a stronger model.
items.soWhat: Unattended agent runs need quality spot-checks, since valid output formats do not prove good work.

items.title: Patrick Collison lets app users request changes an agent then builds
items.takeaway: One user of his personal apps shipped 150 improvements in a few days through an agent-backed box.
items.soWhat: Expect users to want software they can change themselves, and plan for the security and upkeep cost.

items.title: Kun Chen: chatting with agents is the wrong way to create
items.takeaway: His son prefers drawing and recording by hand, disliking the wait and not feeling ownership.
items.soWhat: Chat boxes may limit adoption when people want to feel the work is theirs.

items.title: Karpathy built a full video site with Opus in about two hours
items.takeaway: HackerTube indexes 6,454 YouTube videos recommended in Hacker News comments from 2007 to 2026.
items.soWhat: Data-heavy internal tools that once took a team sprint are now a two-hour build.

items.takeaway: Platform lead Katelyn Lesse describes the Python-to-Rust rebuild on the Latent Space podcast.
items.soWhat: AI can now rewrite core production systems when humans own the design and verification.

voices.quote: This pattern feels like a new kind of tool -- liquid software? -- and every application that doesn't have this feature now has a slightly rigid and anachronistic flavor.
